explanations: luna: The promise that whoever follows God's guidance need not fear or grieve sets a stated good outcome against the section's destructive following of the wretched leader.
terra: People command righteousness while forgetting themselves although they recite the Scripture; this is the boundary between tilawa as mere reading and tilawa embodied by tracing the Book.
terra: After giving Moses the Book, God follows him with successive messengers, again pairing scripture with a properly ordered messenger-chain.
luna: The section's root ت ل و includes recitation and following revealed scripture; this verse speaks of people following what devils recited, a specific contrary use of following a recited account.

luna: The section names ت ل و for reciting and following a revealed book; this verse joins proper recitation of the Book with belief, clarifying the moon's right following as a model for receiving revelation. | terra: يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ makes "true tilawa" the mark of belief, supporting the section's dictionary sense of reading the revealed Book by tracing its form in life.
terra: Abraham asks God to ٱبْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا who will recite His signs; بعث, رسول, and تلاوة converge exactly as they do in the section's account of the sent word.
terra: أَرْسَلْنَا فِيكُمْ رَسُولًا مِّنكُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْكُمْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا gives the إرسال counterpart to 2:129's بعث while retaining the human messenger and recited signs.

luna: When the leaders they followed see the punishment, they disown their followers and their former ties are severed; this gives the section's chief-and-tail relation its judgment-day reversal. | terra: Leaders who were followed disown those who followed them and all bonds are cut; it directly stages the source dictionary's ذنب branch, in which a chief's followers are his "tails."

luna: The followers wish they could return and disown those they followed, just as the leaders disowned them in 2:166; this continues the same account of following a destructive chief. | terra: The followers wish to return so they can disown their leaders, revealing too late the false solidarity of the human following-line described by the section.

luna: When told to follow what God sent down, people insist on the path of their fathers; this is the direct reversal of following the sent message that defines the section's good track. | terra: When told to follow what God has sent down, people choose instead what they found their fathers following; sent revelation and inherited human allegiance compete directly.
terra: God raises prophets as bearers of good news and warning and sends the Book with them, a broad statement of commissioned bearers carrying a revealed word.
terra: God has بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طَالُوتَ مَلِكًا: a leader is raised for the people by God, providing a contrast to the uncommissioned worst man who launches himself.
terra: Saul's followers are tested at the river and only a few remain disciplined; the divinely appointed leader's line is distinguished by obedience under trial.

luna: The section measures following by the moon's course and the Messenger's delivered word; here the Prophet says to follow him, and that following is tested by God's love and forgiveness. | terra: The Messenger is told to say that love of God is shown by following him, giving a positive personal form of following the divinely sent human bearer.
terra: The next command requires obedience to God and the Messenger and marks turning away as disbelief, supplying the negative boundary to 3:31.
terra: The command to travel and see عَـٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ repeats the exact outcome-of-deniers formula highlighted by the section.
terra: God بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِّنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ who recites His signs; divine raising of a human bearer contrasts with Thamud's suspicion of following a human and its man's self-launch.

luna: The verse orders obedience to God, the Messenger, and those in authority, while disputes are referred back to God and the Messenger; it marks a boundary between delegated authority and the self-appointed chief in the section.
luna: The verse says messengers are sent so that they may be obeyed by God's leave (لِيُطَاعَ); it makes the right response to a sent envoy explicit against Thamud's following of their own chief.

luna: Those who obey God and the Messenger are promised company with the prophets and other blessed ones; this gives a positive end to following the envoy, opposite the followers' ruin in the section.

luna: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God; this sets the envoy's authority against the section's people who answer his word by following their self-appointed leader. | terra: Whoever obeys the Messenger obeys God, grounding the messenger's claim to be followed in the Sender rather than in personal rank.
terra: One who opposes the Messenger after guidance is clear and follows a way other than the believers' is left to that choice and enters Hell; messenger and chosen route are inseparable.
terra: Messengers bring good news and warning so people have no argument after them; the ayah defines how a delivered message precedes judgment.
terra: Jesus is sent عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ confirming the Torah before him; messenger and revelation occupy an ordered line of faithful succession.

terra: يَـٰأَيُّهَا ٱلرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ مَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ places the bearer, the borne revelation, and the duty to deliver it together, clarifying the section's paired senses of messenger and message.
terra: The People of the Book are forbidden to follow the desires of a people who went astray, led many astray, and strayed from the level way; leaders and followers share the deviation.
luna: The verse commands obedience to God and the Messenger, then says the Messenger's duty is only clear delivery if people turn away; it repeats the section's message-carrier detail.

luna: The Messenger's duty is only clear delivery; this is a concise formulation of the section's claim that the envoy's burden ends when he hands over the message. | terra: The Messenger's responsibility is only clear delivery, distinguishing faithful carriage of the message from the hearers' responsibility for their response.

luna: People refuse the call to what God sent down and to the Messenger because they rely on their fathers' practice, an explicit competing allegiance. | terra: The call to what God sent down and to the Messenger is answered by preferring ancestral practice, another exact reversal of whom and what should be followed.
terra: The opponents demand that an angel be sent down with the human messenger, restating the false assumption that a human bearer is insufficient.
terra: God says that even an angelic messenger would be made to appear as a man, exposing why the human-form objection cannot identify a false commission.
terra: Again the hearer must travel and look at عَـٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ, turning consequence into the trace by which earlier rejection is read.
luna: The Prophet says he follows only what is revealed to him; this restates the envoy's dependence on a received message rather than a self-started course.
terra: Night is made for rest and sun and moon for reckoning; their measured function connects celestial order to human recognition.
terra: Obeying most people on earth would lead the addressee away from God's way; numerical following supplies no warrant for the direction taken.

luna: When people demand a sign like those given to God's messengers, the verse says God knows where to place His message (رِسَالَتَهُ); the envoy's authority comes from divine choice, unlike the man who launches himself in the section.
terra: Messengers from among the hearers are said to have recited God's signs and warned of the encounter; the addressees acknowledge their own rejection.
terra: God's straight path is to be followed, while other paths are not, because they disperse followers from His way; it abstracts the section's two trajectories into a rule.

luna: Where Thamud reject their envoy and follow their own chief, this verse calls the revealed, blessed Book to be followed, setting the two courses against each other. | terra: The blessed Book is followed by the command فَٱتَّبِعُوهُ; it states plainly that a sent scripture calls for enacted following.
luna: The section contrasts following the sent Messenger with following the most wretched man; this command says to follow what was sent down and not other patrons.
luna: As communities enter the Fire, each curses the community before it; this extends the section's followers-and-leaders relation into a chain of groups that share the end of their course.

luna: After the communities entering the Fire in 7:38, the earlier ones tell the later ones they have no advantage over them and both face punishment; this adds the shared consequence of the follower chain.
luna: Noah says he conveys his Lord's messages (أُبَلِّغُكُمْ رِسَالَاتِ رَبِّي) and advises his people; this repeats the section's messenger-as-carrier and delivered-message detail.
luna: Hud says he conveys his Lord's messages and is a trustworthy adviser; the parallel makes the section's final claim of message-delivery part of repeated prophetic speech.

luna: Salih tells Thamud that God sent him and presents God's she-camel as a sign, opening another account of the envoy rejected in the section. | terra: Salih brings clear proof, names نَاقَةُ ٱللَّهِ a sign, and forbids harming her; it is the fuller messenger-speech compressed in 91:13.

luna: The section's elite reject the sent Salih while common followers trail their chief; here arrogant leaders ask believers whether they know Salih was sent by his Lord, making the social divide explicit. | terra: The arrogant chiefs ask whether Salih is مُرْسَلٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِ, while the believers affirm the message with which he was sent, staging both sender and followers.

luna: The section sets the sent Messenger against the people who follow their wretched chief; these arrogant leaders openly say they disbelieve what the believers believe. | terra: The arrogant chiefs answer the believers by declaring disbelief in the very message the believers affirm, setting the two responses to the sent word side by side.

luna: After the camel and its allotted drink are made a sign, Thamud hamstring it and taunt Salih to bring the threatened punishment if he is a messenger, joining rejection, speech, and action. | terra: After hamstringing the camel, the people challenge Salih to bring the threat إِن كُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ; rejection, deed, and taunt answer the sent messenger.
luna: The earthquake that leaves Thamud fallen in their homes gives the concrete destruction behind the section's claim that the chief led his followers to ruin.

luna: Salih says he delivered his Lord's message and advised them (بَلَّغْتُكُمْ); this directly develops the section's messenger as carrier of a message and its final word about delivery. | terra: Salih's final word, لَقَدْ أَبْلَغْتُكُمْ رِسَالَةَ رَبِّى, distinguishes the faithfully delivered message from the people's refusal to receive it.
luna: Shu'ayb says he conveyed his Lord's messages and advised his people; this repeats the section's specific image of a messenger handing over what he carried.

luna: The Messenger is followed by those who believe and support him; this is the right human-envoy following that contrasts with the crowd who choose their own chief. | terra: Those who believe in the Messenger, support him, and follow the light sent down with him succeed; both the human bearer and the sent word form the rightful following-line.
terra: The universal Messenger commands belief in God and His messenger and says to follow him so that the hearers may be guided, directly naming the rightful following-line.
luna: A man casts off God's signs and Satan pursues him until he becomes lost; the verse reverses the section's proper following, as one who received signs is overtaken by the wrong guide.
luna: The same man inclines to earthly desire and follows his own whim; this specifies the mistaken course following the rejection of signs in 7:175.
luna: When asked for a sign, the Prophet says he follows only what is revealed; this repeats the section's distinction between a sent word and a man's own initiative.

luna: Believers are commanded to obey God and the Messenger and not turn away while hearing him; this makes the proper response to the Messenger's spoken warning explicit. | terra: Believers are told to obey God and His Messenger and not turn away while hearing, joining reception of the spoken word to enacted obedience.
terra: Believers are told to answer God and the Messenger when the Messenger calls them to what gives life, the life-giving opposite of answering a chief who leads to destruction.
terra: When God's signs are recited, opponents claim they could produce the same and call them old tales; their counter-speech is another form of assigning falsehood to the carried word.

luna: Pharaoh's people are drowned after rejecting signs, while the verse says the earlier deniers were seized for their sins (بِذُنُوبِهِمْ); this joins the section's named root ذ ن ب to followers' culpability and ruin. | terra: Like Pharaoh's people before them, deniers are destroyed بِذُنُوبِهِمْ; the shared wording joins collective denial, destructive leadership, and the ordinary "sins" sense of the source section's ذنب.
terra: The sun is radiance and the moon light with measured stations so years and reckoning can be known; their ordered relation makes sequence intelligible to human beings.

luna: The Prophet answers a demand to change revelation by saying he follows only what is revealed; his stance is the reverse of substituting a self-chosen leader's word. | terra: When revelation is recited, opponents demand a different word; the Messenger answers that he only follows what is revealed to him, uniting تلاوة, counter-speech, and faithful following.

luna: Every community has a messenger, and judgment follows when the messenger comes; this repeats the section's sent-to-each-community formulation and its concern with the response. | terra: Every community has a messenger, and when its messenger comes judgment is made justly; it restates the universal sending-and-outcome relation of 16:36.
luna: The Prophet is told to follow what is revealed to him and remain patient until God judges; this is a further explicit statement of the envoy's proper course.
terra: A witness يَتْلُوهُ follows clear proof, while the Book of Moses precedes as guide and mercy; the root ت ل و operates inside a chain of revelation and testimony.
luna: Hud tells his people that if they turn away, he has delivered what he was sent with; this closely parallels Salih's delivered-message ending in 7:79 and the section's carrier image.
terra: Aad disobey their messengers and اتَّبَعُوا أَمْرَ كُلِّ جَبَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ; the ayah exactly repeats the section's two-line structure of rejecting messengers while following a ruinous chief.

luna: Salih is sent to Thamud and calls them to worship God; his mission gives another direct case of the divinely sent envoy set against the self-launched chief in the section. | terra: God sends Thamud their brother Salih, who calls them to their Lord; it restages the human messenger's divine commission and speech.

luna: Thamud answer Salih by recalling their hope in him and objecting to his forbidding their fathers' worship; their response supplies another direct instance of turning from the sent guide. | terra: The people answer Salih that he had inspired hope before he challenged their fathers' worship, exposing inherited allegiance as the rival to his message.
terra: Salih grounds his speech in clear proof and mercy from his Lord and asks who could help him if he disobeyed, defining his own fidelity to the Sender.

luna: Salih identifies the she-camel as a sign and assigns a day of drinking to her and a day to them, giving the warning about God's camel and its drink a fuller parallel. | terra: Salih calls the camel God's sign, tells them to let her feed, and forbids harm, giving the full content of the messenger's command in 91:13.

luna: Thamud hamstring the camel after Salih's warning and are given three days; the act and announced consequence continue the section's camel scene. | terra: After they hamstring her, Salih gives them three days and calls the threat a promise that will not be belied, shifting their charge of lying toward the coming verification.

luna: Salih and the believers are saved from disgrace by God's mercy while the wrongdoers face the outcome; this marks the boundary between following the envoy and the destructive crowd. | terra: When God's command comes, Salih and those who believe with him are saved; correct allegiance separates them from the collective result.

luna: A mighty cry seizes the wrongdoers at daybreak, a specific account of the ruin that follows Thamud's rejection and camel slaughter. | terra: The blast seizes the wrongdoers and leaves them fallen in their homes, the consequence of the deed carried out under their leader.

luna: Thamud are left as though they had never flourished there after denying their Lord; the verse gives the finished result of the section's failed following. | terra: The conclusion names Thamud's denial of their Lord and their removal, making rejection rather than the single man's hand the community's defining act.

luna: The people follow Pharaoh's command, and the verse says his command was not rightly guided; this directly parallels following the section's self-appointed chief over the sent messenger. | terra: Pharaoh's people فَٱتَّبَعُوا أَمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ although his command is not right, a direct parallel to a people taking their destructive leader as the one to follow.

luna: Pharaoh leads his people on the Day of Resurrection to the Fire; the verse states the destination of followers carried by their leader. | terra: Pharaoh يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ and brings them into the Fire: the leader literally goes before his people and determines the destination of those behind him.
terra: A curse is made to follow Pharaoh's people in this life and at resurrection; the repeated following turns the source-section عاقب sense into the consequence trailing the wrong line.

luna: The Day divides people into the wretched (شَقِيٌّ) and the happy (سَعِيدٌ); this gives the section's “most wretched” leader the lexical opposite named in its root gloss. | terra: On the coming day people divide into شَقِىٌّ وَسَعِيدٌ, explicitly confirming the section dictionary's statement that shaqwa stands opposite happiness.

luna: The wretched are assigned the Fire in this continuation of 11:105; it makes explicit the ruin that follows the section's “most wretched” course. | terra: Those classed as wretched in 11:105 are in the Fire here, giving the destination of the source section's شقاوة term.
luna: The Fire's lasting consequence continues the wretched person's fate in 11:106, clarifying what the section's destructive following leads toward.

luna: The happy are placed in the Garden in contrast to the wretched of 11:105–107, giving the section's root ش ق و its stated opposite and a different end. | terra: Those made سُعِدُوا۟ are in the Garden, supplying the positive destination opposite the wretched line.

luna: The Prophet calls to God with insight, “I and whoever follows me” (وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي); this gives the envoy's course and its followers as the opposite of Thamud trailing their chief. | terra: The Messenger identifies his way as calling to God with insight, both for himself and whoever follows him; followers continue the same informed call rather than a chief's blind line.
terra: Sun and moon are subjected and each runs for an appointed term, locating their movement under divine direction rather than self-assertion.
terra: Every messenger is sent in the language of his people so that he can make the message clear, tying divine dispatch to intelligible human speech.

luna: Earlier peoples say their messengers are only humans like them and deny their message; this extends the human-prophet rejection voiced by Thamud. | terra: The verse explicitly includes Thamud among peoples whose messengers brought proofs and who replied that they disbelieved in what the messengers were sent with.

luna: After the prior messenger rejection in 14:9, the messengers reply by asking whether there can be doubt about God, creator of the heavens and earth; this supplies their spoken counterword in that exchange.

luna: The messengers affirm they are indeed humans like their audience, but God grants His favor; this answers the rejection of an envoy because he is human. | terra: The messengers acknowledge that they are humans like their hearers but say God favors whom He wills; divine sending, rather than species, establishes whom to follow.

luna: The weak followers and arrogant leaders face one another at judgment, exposing the social structure behind a crowd's choice to follow its chief. | terra: The weak followers ask the arrogant leaders whether they can avert any punishment; the exchange exposes the impotence of the "heads" whose "tails" followed them.

luna: Satan says he only invited people and they answered him, refusing their blame; this preserves the followers' responsibility even when misled. | terra: Satan tells his followers that he merely called and they responded, then disowns their attempt to blame him; the speech lays bare agency within a ruinous following-line.
terra: God subjects the sun and moon as two beings continually running their courses, reinforcing the regular service implicit in the moon's following.
terra: God sent messengers among the communities of earlier peoples, establishing the repeated historical setting for the next ayah's response.
terra: No messenger came without being mocked, giving the recurrent rejection enacted specifically by Thamud's taunts to Salih.
luna: The section pairs a messenger sent with a people who deny him; this parallel says the people of al-Hijr denied the messengers.
luna: Though clear signs came to the people of al-Hijr, they turned away from them; this supplies a further account of refusing the envoy's warning.
luna: The punishment cry seizes the people of al-Hijr at morning, continuing the section's pattern in which rejection of the messenger ends in destruction.
luna: What the people of al-Hijr had earned does not avail them after the blast; the verse specifies that their own course cannot shield the deniers from its end.

luna: Those who mislead others carry their own burdens and some of the burdens of those they misled; this gives the section's leader-and-followers relation a shared moral consequence. | terra: Those who mislead others carry their own full burdens and some burdens of people led without knowledge, showing how a leader's offense extends through the followers he recruits.

luna: Immediately before 16:36's sending of a messenger to every community, this verse asks whether the messengers have any duty beyond clear delivery; it states the section's delivered-message claim.

luna: The section itself pairs the root ب ع ث (“send”) with ر س ل: this verse says a messenger was sent to every community to call against false gods, then distinguishes guided from doomed rejecters and says to look at the deniers' end. | terra: The section explicitly joins this ayah's بَعَثْنَا ... رَسُولًا to 91:12: God raises a messenger in every community, whereas Thamud's worst man launches himself; the same ayah then directs attention to the deniers' outcome.
terra: وَمَا كُنَّا مُعَذِّبِينَ حَتَّىٰ نَبْعَثَ رَسُولًا sets a firm boundary: punishment follows only after God has raised a messenger.

luna: The verse names Thamud's she-camel as a visible sign they wronged and connects signs with warning; it directly places the section's camel episode among God's warnings. | terra: God gives Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wrong her; the ayah explains that sent signs warn, linking the messenger's object to its purpose.
luna: Every people is called with its imam (بِإِمَامِهِمْ), an afterlife image of a following gathered under a leader; imam can mean a leader or a record here, so the parallel remains uncertain.

luna: People say they would not believe unless a human messenger were sent; the verse directly reverses the section's rejected human envoy and names the objection. | terra: People reject guidance by asking whether God has sent a human as messenger; the ayah identifies the same false premise behind Thamud's question.
terra: The reply says that if angels dwelt securely on earth, an angel messenger would be sent; human messengers fit human addressees, reversing the people's objection.

terra: The sleepers deliberately send one of their own to the city with money and instructions for care; this benign group commission contrasts with Thamud's uncommissioned worst man and the companion summoned to offend.

luna: The section names ت ل و as reciting revealed scripture and following its trace; here the Prophet is told to recite what was revealed from his Lord's Book, sharpening that recitation-following link.
terra: The Messenger is told not to obey one whose heart neglects remembrance and who follows desire, a boundary against allowing a disordered person to set the line.
terra: Jesus says God did not make him a domineering wretch, جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا; a divinely commissioned speaker is expressly separated from the wretched tyrant type that people wrongly follow.

luna: God says the Qur'an was not sent down to make the Prophet wretched; this contrasts the sent guidance with the wretched leader named in the section. | terra: The Quran is not sent down لِتَشْقَىٰ; the revelation that should be followed is expressly dissociated from the شقاوة embodied by Thamud's worst man.
luna: The Qur'an is a reminder for the one who fears, which supplies the responsive stance opposed to Thamud's rejection of the warning.

luna: The verse says Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them; this is an explicit counterpart to the section's leader who takes the people after him toward ruin. | terra: وَأَضَلَّ فِرْعَوْنُ قَوْمَهُ وَمَا هَدَى names the result of corrupt leadership: Pharaoh leads his people away rather than guiding them.

luna: Whoever follows God's guidance is promised not to go astray or be wretched; it is the explicit opposite of following the section's most wretched leader. | terra: Whoever follows divine guidance فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ; correct following is expressly protected from both straying and the شقاوة embodied by Thamud's worst man.
terra: Turning away from God's reminder brings a constricted life and blind resurrection, completing the negative side of 20:123's promise to one who follows guidance.
terra: Night, day, sun, and moon each swim in an orbit; the same celestial objects display rule-governed movement rather than destructive competition.
terra: Messengers before Muhammad were mocked, and the very warning mocked came to surround the mockers; rejection and outcome turn back upon the speakers.
luna: The prophets are made leaders guiding by God's command; this gives the positive, divinely directed counterpart to the section's leader who carries followers to ruin.
terra: A person disputes about God without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil, identifying a destructive speaker with the leader he follows.
terra: It is decreed that whoever takes that rebellious devil as guide will be led astray and guided to the Blaze, a direct leader-follower-result sequence.
terra: Thamud are explicitly included among earlier peoples who denied, placing their response within the repeated history of communities rejecting warning.
luna: God chooses messengers from angels and people (يَصْطَفِي); the verse clarifies that the messenger is appointed, the opposite of the self-appointed chief who rises in the section.

luna: The deniers say the messenger is only a human like them and warn that obeying him would make them losers; this repeats the human-following objection voiced by Thamud. | terra: Noah's elite reject a human like themselves, accuse him of seeking superiority, and claim that God would have sent angels; their argument closely matches Thamud's refusal to follow one human.
terra: The chiefs call the human messenger a possessed man and tell the people to wait him out, completing the accusatory speech begun in 23:24.

luna: The deniers object that the messenger is only a human like themselves and accuse him of falsehood; this repeats the contempt for following one human voiced in 54:24. | terra: The elite describe their messenger as a mortal who eats and drinks like the people; this is the premise for their warning in 23:34 against obeying a human like themselves.

luna: They warn that obeying a human like themselves would mean loss; the verse makes explicit the anti-human-messenger argument behind rejecting Salih. | terra: The chiefs claim that obeying a human like themselves would make the people losers, nearly restating Thamud's scorn at following one human from among them.
luna: The deniers call their messenger a man who invented a lie against God; this parallels the section's false accusation against the envoy they should follow.

luna: Messengers are sent one after another to their peoples, who deny them and are made tales; this expands the section's sequence of sending, denial, and consequence. | terra: God sends messengers تَتْرَا, every community rejects its messenger, and He makes the communities follow one another into ruin; sending, denial, succession, and result occupy one ayah.
terra: The condemned say غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا and admit they were astray, joining wretchedness to the path they collectively took.

luna: The Prophet is told to say that obeying him is guidance; this names the right result of following the messenger whose spoken warning Thamud reject. | terra: أَطِيعُوا۟ ٱلرَّسُولَ and فَإِن تُطِيعُوهُ تَهْتَدُوا۟ make obedience to the messenger the route to guidance, while his own duty is clear delivery.

luna: The deniers object that the messenger eats food and walks in markets; this repeats the human-messenger objection that underlies Thamud's “one human” question. | terra: Opponents ask what sort of messenger eats food and walks in markets, another specific rejection of a human bearer on the basis of shared humanity.
luna: They ask why an angel was not sent with the human messenger; this continues the objection to following an envoy from among themselves.

luna: Earlier messengers are said to have eaten food and walked in markets; this answers the contempt for a human envoy voiced by the section's Thamud. | terra: God answers that earlier messengers also ate food and walked in markets and made people a trial for one another; ordinary humanity is part of the sending, not a reason to reject it.

luna: On the Day of Judgment, a follower regrets not taking a path with the Messenger; this makes the section's choice between following the envoy and another leader's path concrete. | terra: The wrongdoer regrets not having taken a path with the Messenger, locating the fatal choice precisely between the sent guide and another companion.
luna: The regretful follower calls his companion a misleader who turned him away from the Reminder, a close counterpart to people following the section's destructive chief.

luna: The speaker says the companion made him forget the Reminder after it came; this identifies what the wrong follower's influence displaced. | terra: The chosen companion "led me away from the Reminder after it came to me," a compact parallel to following a man who diverts one from the messenger's word.
terra: God makes night and day a succession, خِلْفَةً, for one who wishes to remember or give thanks; orderly alternation becomes an ethical invitation.
luna: The prayer asks God to make its speakers leaders for the God-fearing; it presents leadership as serving right guidance, opposite the section's destructive chief.

terra: Moses and Aaron say إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ with a singular رسول for their joint commission; this can reflect the source dictionary's message/commission sense alongside its bearer sense.

luna: The section cites this statement that Thamud denied the messengers; its root ك ذ ب and plural envoy frame are the exact rejection at the center of the image. | terra: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ gives the section's compressed formulation: Thamud assigns falsehood to the sent messengers.

luna: Salih asks Thamud whether they will not fear God, a spoken warning that parallels the Messenger's address before they answer with denial. | terra: Salih's opening question, asking whether Thamud will be mindful, initiates the messenger's direct address before he identifies himself in 26:143.

luna: Salih calls himself a trustworthy messenger (رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ); this directly joins the section's account of the sent messenger and the people who reject his word. | terra: Salih's إِنِّى لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ is the messenger's own counterword: the man they reject identifies himself as a trustworthy bearer.

luna: Salih commands the people to fear God and obey him; this is the right following that stands against their obedience to their own chief. | terra: فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ is Salih's direct claim to rightful obedience, the alternative to following the people's chosen offender.
terra: Salih says that he asks no payment for his message, supplying a concrete reason to obey the trustworthy messenger rather than the people's self-interested chiefs.

luna: Salih again says to fear God and obey him, repeating the envoy's instruction at the point where the account turns to the transgressing leaders. | terra: Salih repeats فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ immediately before naming the rival command not to obey.

luna: Salih tells them not to obey the transgressors (الْمُسْرِفِينَ); this names the wrong course that the section depicts when the people follow their most wretched man. | terra: وَلَا تُطِيعُوا۟ أَمْرَ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ explicitly draws the boundary between obedience to Salih and obedience to the transgressing leaders.

luna: The transgressors spread corruption in the land and do not set things right; this specifies why the leaders whom the people follow are destructive. | terra: The leaders whom Salih says not to obey spread corruption and do not set things right, explaining what their followers participate in.

luna: Thamud answer Salih by accusing him of being bewitched, another spoken dismissal of the envoy after his warning. | terra: Thamud call Salih one of the bewitched immediately before objecting that he is only human; this ayah contributes their first counterword to the messenger's command.

luna: They say Salih is only a human like them and demand a sign; this directly parallels their contempt for following one person in 54:24, before the camel sign is stated. | terra: Thamud reply that Salih is only a human like them and demand a sign, directly repeating their objection to following one human messenger.

luna: Salih assigns the she-camel a known day's drink (شِرْبٌ) and the people their day's drink, a precise parallel to the section's phrase about God's camel and its watering. | terra: Salih identifies the camel and assigns her and the people separate drinking days, expanding the watering claim of 91:13.

luna: Salih forbids them to harm the camel lest the punishment seize them; this gives the warning attached to its water and the cost of rejecting it. | terra: Salih forbids touching the camel with harm and warns of a tremendous day's punishment, so the consequence is stated before the choice.

luna: They hamstring the camel (فَعَقَرُوهَا), the exact deed of the section's Thamud scene. | terra: They hamstring the camel and then become regretful, showing the community's participation in the chosen agent's deed.

luna: The punishment seizes Thamud after the slaughter; this explicitly joins the action to the ruin of the followers. | terra: The threatened punishment seizes them, completing this account's message-rejection-result line.
luna: The camel episode remains a sign, yet most do not believe; the verse closes this messenger-and-followers account with the same split between warning and response.
luna: The people tell their messenger he is a human like them and accuse him of lying; this repeats the section's linked rejection of a human envoy and false charge.

luna: Salih is sent to Thamud, who divide into two disputing groups; this repeats the section's divinely sent messenger and shows the community splitting over him. | terra: God sends Salih to Thamud, after which they become two factions disputing; the sent word immediately exposes opposed lines within the people.
terra: Salih asks why his people hasten evil before good and urges them to seek forgiveness; it supplies the messenger's warning to which their evil-omen accusation in 27:47 replies.
terra: They attribute their evil omen to Salih and his companions; he answers that their omen is with God, another word-against-word form of rejecting the messenger.

luna: Nine men in the city are identified as a corrupt faction; this is the specific inner circle the section points to within the wider body of followers. | terra: The تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ who corrupt the city expose the organized core around Thamud's worst man, clarifying how a collective follows a destructive head.

luna: The nine swear to attack Salih and his family at night and then deny responsibility; the verse shows the chief-following faction actively plotting against the envoy. | terra: The nine conspirators swear together to attack Salih and his family and then lie about witnessing it, displaying the destructive leadership group's coordinated action and speech.

luna: The plotters devise a scheme while God counters it without their awareness; this reverses the self-directed plan that replaces the messenger's instruction. | terra: Their plot meets God's counter-plan while they are unaware, marking the boundary between self-directed human scheming and divine disposal.

luna: The verse tells the listener to see the end of their plot and their destruction; this supplies the consequence for the corrupt inner circle named in 27:48. | terra: The reader is told to look at the عَـٰقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ: the consequence of the leaders' plot is their destruction with their people.

luna: Their houses lie empty because of their wrongdoing, a visible aftermath of the course the section says the chief and followers take. | terra: Their houses lie empty because of their wrongdoing, making the wrong following-line's collective end visible in the landscape.

luna: God saves those who believed and feared Him from the city's destruction; this marks the distinct outcome of following rightly. | terra: God saves those who believed and were mindful, preserving the opposite community from the one organized around the nine corrupters.

luna: Pharaoh's people are made leaders who invite others to the Fire; this is an explicit reversal of the envoy's invitation, matching the section's destructive leader and his followers. | terra: God makes Pharaoh's party leaders who call to the Fire; the ayah states in general form what the section shows through a chief who takes those behind him to ruin.
terra: A curse is made to follow those leaders in this world and disgrace follows on resurrection, extending the leader-follower chain into its outcome.
terra: Failure to answer the messenger reveals that the opponents follow their desires, and the ayah asks who is more astray than one who follows desire without divine guidance.
terra: God does not destroy towns until He has sent a messenger to their center reciting His signs; the ayah fixes the ethical order of message, rejection, and consequence.
terra: Disbelievers tell believers ٱتَّبِعُوا سَبِيلَنَا and falsely offer to carry their sins; this is a chief's seductive counterword inviting the wrong following-line.

luna: Those who mislead others will carry their own burdens and burdens with theirs; the verse spells out the consequences of leading followers astray. | terra: The inviters will carry their own burdens and burdens added to them, exposing the consequence hidden by their promise to prospective followers.
luna: The verse says earlier peoples also denied messengers and that the Messenger's duty is only clear delivery; it joins repeated rejection to the section's final delivery detail.
luna: The verse names Thamud and says Satan made their deeds seem fair and barred them from the path; this gives a specific account of the false course behind their rejection of the warning.
terra: The command to recite what has been revealed is followed by prayer's restraint from wrong, linking the spoken tilawa of scripture to an embodied moral trace.
terra: God يُرْسِلُ ٱلرِّيَـٰحَ, they raise clouds, and He spreads them through the sky; physical sending becomes motion and extension, the source section's named ر س ل root sense.

luna: When told to follow what God revealed, people answer that they will follow what they found their fathers doing; this restates the contrast between revealed guidance and inherited following. | terra: People refuse the command to follow what God sent down and choose their fathers even when Satan is inviting them to the Blaze, exposing the destination of the rival line.
terra: God makes night enter day and day enter night and subjects sun and moon, each running to a fixed term; ordered alternation frames the same celestial pair.
luna: God makes patient, certain people leaders guiding by His command; this is a specific reversal of the chief who rises on his own and leads followers astray.
terra: Once God and His Messenger decide a matter, believers have no competing choice; disobedience is named clear error, fixing the authority of the sent bearer over rival human preference.
luna: The damned wish they had obeyed God and the Messenger; this states the lost alternative to following the self-appointed leader.

luna: The condemned say they obeyed their chiefs and great ones, who turned them from the path; this is the wrong following the section stages. | terra: The condemned admit أَطَعْنَا سَادَتَنَا وَكُبَرَاءَنَا فَأَضَلُّونَا ٱلسَّبِيلَا, making explicit how chiefs and great men lead their followers off the way.
luna: They ask God to double punishment for those chiefs; the following relationship has a shared consequence, like the section's chief and his people destroyed together.

luna: The deniers refuse to believe the Qur'an and earlier scriptures; the verse then places weak followers before the arrogant group they followed, staging the competing allegiances in the section. | terra: The weak tell the arrogant that without them they would have believed, a judgment-day disclosure of how social leaders blocked the sent word.

luna: The arrogant deny that they forced the weak away after revelation came; this adds the leaders' part in diverting followers from the sent word. | terra: The arrogant ask whether they forcibly barred guidance after it came, preserving the leaders' attempt to evade responsibility for their influence.

luna: The weak confess that their leaders commanded them to disbelieve; the mutual blame clarifies the followers' tie to those who misled them. | terra: The weak answer that the leaders' night-and-day scheming commanded disbelief, and both sides conceal regret when punishment appears; followers and chiefs share the result.
terra: Whenever a warner is sent to a town, its affluent leaders declare disbelief in the message, generalizing the role played by Thamud's leading group.
terra: وَمَا يُمْسِكْ فَلَا مُرْسِلَ لَهُ directly realizes the section's dictionary statement that إرسال is the opposite of إمساك: what God withholds no one can release.
terra: The same joining of night and day and appointed courses of sun and moon repeats the rule-governed cosmic line against which human following is measured.

luna: Every community has had a warner; this is a close formulation of the section's point that a messenger is sent to each people. | terra: No community is without a warner, supporting the section's universal horizon for the sent bearer beyond Salih and Thamud.
terra: Earlier peoples deny messengers even though their bearers bring clear proofs, scriptures, and the illuminating Book, joining the carrier to the carried word.
terra: God then seizes those who disbelieve; this ayah supplies the result of the messenger-denial scene stated in 35:25.
luna: The one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen is promised forgiveness and generous reward; this states the receptive response opposite Thamud's rejection.

luna: A people answer their messengers, “You are only humans like us,” and call them liars; this joins the section's human-envoy objection to its accusation of falsehood. | terra: The town rejects its messengers as mere humans and says they are lying, reproducing Thamud's objection while marking it as the unbelievers' response.
terra: A man comes running from the farthest part of the city and says ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ; this self-mobilized man's righteous intervention reverses Thamud's worst man's initiative.
terra: ٱتَّبِعُوا۟ مَن لَّا يَسْـَٔلُكُمْ أَجْرًا وَهُم مُّهْتَدُونَ supplies the explicit reason to follow the messengers: they seek no payment and are themselves guided.
terra: The sun runs toward its appointed limit by divine determination, providing the ordered first member of the sun-moon sequence completed in 36:39-40.

luna: The moon is assigned successive phases until it returns like an old palm stalk; 36:40 then sets the sun and moon's ordered relation, completing the lunar sequence relevant to 91:2. | terra: The moon is assigned measured phases, supplying the second celestial body whose course 36:40 protects from collision or overtaking.

luna: The sun cannot overtake the moon and night does not outrun day; this gives the celestial order behind 91:2 its explicit boundary and clarifies that following preserves sequence. | terra: The sun cannot overtake the moon and night cannot outstrip day; each travels in an orbit, supplying the ordered celestial succession against which the section measures human following.
terra: God's covenant forbids serving Satan because he is a manifest enemy, establishing the prohibition before naming the multitudes he led astray.
terra: The command to worship God is identified as the straight path, supplying the rightful course opposite Satan's following-line.
terra: Satan has led a great multitude astray; the hearers are asked why they did not reason, exposing the scale of following as no defense for its direction.
luna: On the Day, the followers turn to one another in accusation; this stages the afterlife reckoning of those who shared a mistaken course.

luna: In the mutual accusation begun in 37:27, one side says the other came “from the right” (عَنِ الْيَمِينِ); the phrase's force is uncertain, so this adds only the followers' dispute with those they followed.
luna: The accused answer that the followers were not believers; the verse continues the dispute between the crowd and those it followed.
luna: The leaders deny having authority over the followers and call them transgressors; the verse identifies their shared responsibility and the followers' agency.
luna: The word of punishment is said to have come true for both parties; this connects their bad following to its result.

luna: The leaders admit they themselves were astray and led others astray; this states the section's destructive leadership relation directly. | terra: The leaders admit that they led the others astray because they themselves were astray, an explicit confession of the destructive line represented by Thamud's worst man.

luna: The verse says both will share the punishment that day, completing the consequence of leader and followers in 37:27–32. | terra: Leaders and followers share the punishment, giving the consequence of the admitted misguidance in 37:32.

luna: The rejecters are found following the tracks of their fathers, a direct case of pursuing predecessors instead of the sent warning. | terra: They found their fathers astray, identifying that the inherited leaders were already off course.

luna: They rush along those tracks (يُهْرَعُونَ), giving the section's followers-of-the-chief image a repeated form in the ancestral path they imitate. | terra: They are made to hurry عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِم, a vivid wrong succession that enacts the section's عاقب gloss of coming in another's tracks.
terra: Night is wrapped over day and day over night while sun and moon each run to a stated term, giving another measured celestial succession.

luna: The praised listeners hear speech and follow its best (فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُ); this is a positive counterpart to the crowd that answers the Messenger's speech with denial. | terra: Those who listen to the word and follow its best are the ones God guides, giving the positive reception of a carried saying that Thamud refuses.
terra: God withholds the souls whose death He decrees and يُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ until a term; the bodily scene gives another concrete Quranic realization of إرسال against إمساك.

luna: The command to follow what was sent down before punishment comes is the clear alternative to the Thamud who ignore their envoy's warning. | terra: The hearer is commanded to follow the best of what has been sent down before punishment comes suddenly, preserving the section's order of word, response, and result.

luna: The deniers are driven in groups to Hell after warnings came; this echoes the section's crowd moving together to destruction after rejecting the messenger. | terra: At Hell's gates the keepers ask whether messengers from among the condemned recited God's signs and warned them; the answer admits the warning and its realized result.
luna: Those who feared their Lord are led in groups to the Garden after messengers and warning; it gives the other destination for a community's response.
terra: Every community schemes to seize its messenger and disputes with falsehood; God then seizes it, reproducing the section's messenger-denial-deed-result sequence.
terra: A believing man from Pharaoh's household stands up to defend Moses because he says "My Lord is God" and has brought proofs; his initiative reverses the worst man's leadership in Thamud.
terra: The believing man says "follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct," making a righteous self-mobilized human voice the opposite of a chief who guides his people to ruin.
terra: The believer sets the two calls side by side: he calls his people to salvation while they call him to the Fire, exactly articulating opposed following-lines.
terra: He explains that they call him to disbelief while he calls them to the Mighty, Forgiving God; this ayah supplies the contents and destinations of the rival invitations.
terra: In the Fire the weak ask the arrogant leaders to relieve part of the punishment because they had been followers, realizing the section's "tails of chiefs" image.
terra: The arrogant answer that all are in the Fire and judgment is settled, showing that leadership cannot save the people it drew behind it.

luna: Thamud prefer blindness after guidance comes and are seized for what they earned; this is the section's wrong following and its outcome. | terra: God guides Thamud, but they prefer blindness over guidance, and the thunderbolt takes them; their wrong preference gives the inner form of the false following-line.

luna: Those who believed and feared God are saved; beside Thamud's fate, this gives the other outcome of following the warning. | terra: God saves those who believe and remain mindful, completing the direct contrast to Thamud's preference for blindness in 41:17.
luna: If people turn away, the Messenger is not their keeper and has only to deliver clearly; this develops the section's claim that his burden is to convey, even when followers refuse.
luna: They call the inherited religion of their fathers a community they follow; this gives the wrong-following side a second explicit ancestral formulation.

luna: People choose to follow their fathers' inherited way over the messenger's invitation, another stated reversal of the section's right following. | terra: Whenever a warner is sent, affluent leaders say they found their fathers on a way and follow their traces; the chiefs articulate inherited following against divine sending.

luna: When a messenger offers better guidance, the people insist on following their fathers; this makes the rejection of a sent guide explicit. | terra: Even when the warner offers better guidance than the ancestral path, the leaders declare disbelief in what he was sent with, joining wrong following to explicit rejection.

luna: Pharaoh misleads his people and they obey him, directly reversing the order in which the sent Messenger should be followed. | terra: Pharaoh makes light of his people فَأَطَاعُوهُ; their obedience to a defiantly corrupt head closely matches Thamud's following of its worst member.
terra: One who hears God's signs recited yet persists arrogantly as though unheard receives a painful warning, connecting recitation, refusal, and outcome.
luna: The Prophet is set on a law and told to follow it rather than the desires of those without knowledge; this makes explicit the difference between received guidance and self-chosen direction.
luna: The Prophet says he follows only what is revealed and is only a clear warner; this joins the received message to the envoy's role in the section.
terra: Disbelievers follow falsehood while believers follow the truth from their Lord; one ayah explicitly lays out the two opposed following-lines that structure the section.
terra: Believers are forbidden to put themselves ahead of God and His Messenger, a positional rule that prevents a human will from taking the head of the revelatory line.

luna: Thamud are told to enjoy themselves for a short time before their rebellion in 51:44; this is the warning-and-delay immediately preceding the end of the same people. | terra: Thamud are told to enjoy themselves only until a stated time, placing a measured warning before their final refusal.

luna: Thamud arrogantly rebel against their Lord's command, then the thunderbolt seizes them as they look; this joins refusal of the warning to its immediate consequence. | terra: They insolently defy their Lord's command and the thunderbolt takes them while they look on, joining rejected command and result.

luna: They cannot stand up or help themselves after the thunderbolt in 51:44; this completes the destruction of the Thamud whose rejection the section depicts. | terra: After the punishment they cannot even rise or help themselves; their inability to stand forms a pointed aftermath to the self-rising ٱنۢبَعَثَ of 91:12.

terra: Wrongdoers have a ذَنُوبًا, an allotted share like that of their companions; this distinct Quranic sense of the source section's ذنب root makes shared consequence itself the followers' portion.

luna: This passage says Thamud denied the warnings; it directly names the rejection that opens the section's account of their chief and his followers. | terra: ثَمُودُ بِٱلنُّذُرِ opens the parallel account with Thamud's denial of warnings, identifying what the following human objection rejects in 54:24.

luna: The question “shall we follow one human from among us?” (نَتَّبِعُهُ) names the refusal to follow Salih, directly opposed to following the divine envoy. | terra: Thamud's أَبَشَرًا مِّنَّا وَاحِدًا نَّتَّبِعُهُ states the section's decisive refusal: they scorn following the one human messenger they ought to follow.

luna: They call him an arrogant liar (كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ), the counterword to the messenger's trustworthy warning in the section. | terra: Their reply calls the bearer of the reminder كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ, enacting the section's كذب sense of assigning a lie to the messenger.

luna: The deniers are told they will know who the liar is tomorrow; this turns their false accusation toward the consequence of rejecting the envoy. | terra: The answer to Thamud's accusation says that tomorrow they will know who is the insolent liar; this ayah reverses the charge in 54:25 before the camel trial begins.

luna: God sends the she-camel as a trial and commands patience with them; this directly develops the sign and test implicit in the section's camel-and-drink warning. | terra: God is مُرْسِلُوا۟ ٱلنَّاقَةِ as a trial and commands watchfulness and patience; the camel is itself sent into the contested obedience scene.

luna: the verse says to tell them that the water is divided between them, each receiving a turn; this is the exact scene behind the Messenger's brief “camel of God and its drink.” | terra: The water is divided and each turn is attended, supplying the exact watering-right carried in Salih's message in 91:13.

luna: They call their companion, who takes the deed upon himself and hamstrings the camel (فَتَعَاطَىٰ فَعَقَرَ); this is the section's self-appointed man acting for the crowd. | terra: The people call their صَاحِب, and that single chosen man undertakes the deed and hamstrings the camel; this is the wrong earthly following-line described in the section.

luna: This adjacent warning names the punishment after the camel slaughter in 54:29, completing the deed-to-consequence link in the section. | terra: فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ answers the people's taunt by joining the rejected warnings to their realized outcome.

luna: The single blast destroys them like dry stalks after 54:30's warning; this gives the followers' destruction a concrete end. | terra: The single blast leaves the people like dry pen-fodder, completing the consequence of following the companion who hamstrung the camel.
terra: ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ states that sun and moon move by calculation, reinforcing the measured order behind the moon's following.
terra: God sends messengers with clear proofs and sends down the Book and balance so people may uphold justice; the dispatched bearers carry a word intended to shape conduct.
terra: God causes messengers to follow عَلَىٰٓ ءَاثَـٰرِهِمْ after Noah and Abraham, a righteous succession that exactly enacts the source-section عاقب gloss of coming in another's trace.
terra: Moses asks why his people harm him although they know he is God's messenger; when they deviate, their hearts are made to deviate, linking treatment of the messenger to direction.
terra: Jesus identifies himself as God's messenger, confirms the preceding scripture, and announces a later messenger; when clear proofs arrive, the hearers dismiss them as magic.
terra: بَعَثَ فِى ٱلْأُمِّيِّـۧنَ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِ again binds divine commissioning, a messenger from among the people, and recitation.
terra: Those charged with the Torah but failing to bear it are likened to a donkey carrying books; the image distinguishes possession of revelation from living in its trace.
terra: When messengers bring clear proofs, people ask whether humans will guide them, then disbelieve and turn away; the objection and its consequence mirror Thamud's choice.
luna: The verse commands obedience to God and the Messenger, then says that if people turn away, the Messenger's duty is only clear delivery; this repeats the section's carrier-and-message claim.
terra: The inhabitants of the Fire admit that a warner came but they denied him and said God had sent nothing; their own words connect rejected sending to the outcome.

luna: The passage says Thamud and Aad denied the striking calamity; Thamud's denial repeats the section's ك ذ ب rejection before its account of the camel. | terra: Thamud and Aad deny the striking calamity, reducing the same historical scene to denial of the announced event.

luna: Thamud are destroyed by the overwhelming blast; the verse supplies another concise account of the fate following their denial. | terra: Thamud are destroyed by the overwhelming blast, supplying the result that follows the denial named in 69:4.

luna: The section's root ر س ل allows “messenger” for the borne word as well as its carrier; this verse calls the revelation the speech of a noble messenger (قَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ), linking message and bearer. | terra: The Quran is called قَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ, placing "word" and "messenger" together and illuminating the section's distinction between the carried saying and its carrier.
terra: God discloses the unseen only to an approved messenger and stations guards before and behind him, protecting the transmission that 72:28 says is delivered.
terra: The purpose is to establish that the messengers أَبْلَغُوا۟ رِسَـٰلَـٰتِ رَبِّهِمْ; borne messages and their bearers are distinguished yet joined.

luna: The moon is darkened immediately before 75:9 joins the sun and moon; this marks the breakdown of the distinct celestial course in which the moon follows the sun. | terra: The moon is darkened before sun and moon are joined in 75:9, beginning the end-time reversal of the luminous, ordered following seen in the section.

luna: The sun and moon are joined at the Resurrection, a boundary that reverses the separate, ordered relation pictured by the moon following the sun in 91:2. | terra: The sun and moon are brought together at the end, a specific boundary and reversal of the ordered succession represented by the moon following the sun.
terra: فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ فَٱتَّبِعْ قُرْءَانَهُ joins recitation and following in one command, precisely supporting the section's tilawa as both reading and conforming to revelation.
terra: وَٱلْمُرْسَلَـٰتِ عُرْفًا evokes beings or winds sent forth in ordered succession, bringing the section's sending and following motifs into one compact image.
terra: Within the sequence begun by the sent ones of 77:1, these agents cast a reminder; this ayah supplies the borne word that completes that neighbouring dispatch scene.

luna: Like 69:40, this verse calls the revelation the speech of a noble messenger (قَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ); it concretely joins the delivered word to the one who carries it, with the messenger's identity depending on the passage's context. | terra: Again revelation is قَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ, here in a passage describing a powerful, obeyed, trustworthy bearer; the message reaches its hearer through a commissioned carrier.
terra: The reminder is avoided by ٱلْأَشْقَى, joining the superlative "most wretched" to refusal of the very word one should heed.

luna: This next verse says the person who avoids the reminder in 87:11 will enter the great Fire; it supplies that wretched person's consequence. | terra: That most-wretched person enters the great Fire, giving the outcome of avoiding the reminder.
luna: The next verse says the person there neither dies nor lives, completing the lasting consequence of the wretched person's avoidance of the reminder in 87:11–12.

luna: The Fire is entered by the most wretched one (الْأَشْقَى), repeating the section's word for its self-starting leader in an explicit punishment setting. | terra: The Fire is entered by ٱلْأَشْقَى, repeating the section's superlative for the most wretched and attaching it to the ultimate result.

luna: The one who denies and turns away is distinguished from the God-fearing recipient of guidance in 92:17; this is the section's choice between rejecting the envoy and following rightly. | terra: ٱلَّذِى كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ defines that "most wretched" person by denial and turning away, the same moral sequence as Thamud's rejection.
luna: The God-fearing are kept away from the Fire in contrast to the wretched of 92:15–16, clarifying the other side of the section's moral divide.
